previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes and a history of gastroparesis, diabetic retinopathy, chronic kidney disease, and depression was admitted for nausea, vomiting, and altered mental status due to a gastroparesis flare. She presented with hyperglycemia, hypertension, and lethargy but improved with IV fluids, insulin adjustment, and symptom management. Her mental status normalized, she tolerated a full diet, and her vitals stabilized. She was discharged home on adjusted insulin therapy with plans for follow-up in endocrinology, gastroenterology, nephrology, and psychiatry. Key issues included uncontrolled diabetes with neurological and ophthalmic manifestations, gastroparesis, hypertensive chronic kidney disease, anemia, and depressive disorder.
problems: Diabetes with neurological manifestations, type I [juvenile type], uncontrolled
Diabetes with ophthalmic manifestations, type I [juvenile type], uncontrolled
Hypertensive chronic kidney disease, benign, with chronic kidney disease stage I through stage IV, or unspecified
